study.question: After making the shared history-selector trunk click-owned, do auxiliary losses help or interfere through the remaining shared embedding updates, and does ownership differ between user/context and item/history/action field groups?
study.hypothesis: The incumbent still allows auxiliary losses into shared embeddings through context/target tower inputs and pooled history values, although auxiliary score inputs are detached. A forward-shared but click-owned backward boundary on one or both field groups may improve click ranking without new capacity. This is a test of task-to-parameter ownership, not evidence that auxiliary information is intrinsically harmful. Auxiliary tasks continue to see the full representation and train their own score rows and towers; historical feedback remains available to click.

nearest_work.difference: Exact forward/initialization parent. Its primary selector still leaves auxiliary context, target and history-value embedding paths live. This study gates those remaining backward paths in a 2x2 factorial; no new modules.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/2308.13537v2 (Su et al., STEM, Method and feature-field ablations)
nearest_work.difference: STEM combines shared and task-specific embedding tables and experts with stop-gradient cross-task transfer. Here one table per field is retained and auxiliary ownership is switched by field group. This is a diagnostic adaptation of established backward routing, not a STEM reproduction or verified novel mechanism.

INFNet uses task/category/sequence tokens and proxy-guided interactions. No proxies, task tokens or new forward interaction block are adopted here; this study isolates backward ownership in the existing local-activation network.

Inherits the local target/history interaction and four-task field adaptation through the incumbent. Initial DIN remains the empirical anchor, while the exact incumbent is the matched architecture control.

inherited_components: Entire g3-r0002-wide_primary constructor, parameter topology, reset order and tied initial score-readout rows; candidate.py was byte-identical to its archived source before editing.
Target-conditioned unnormalized local-activation pooling over actual masked item/history fields plus historical action values; current target action is never consumed.
Shared field embeddings, separate task readout rows and task towers, primary-only nonlinear selector gradient routing, fixed host loss and training recipe.
Established stop-gradient/backward-routing idea from STEM; field-wise ownership is tested without introducing its multiple embedding tables or experts.
study.proposed_difference: Add two parameter-free switches: block_aux_context_gradient detaches context before auxiliary towers; block_aux_item_gradient detaches target before auxiliary towers and substitutes bmm(auxiliary_scores, values.detach()) for auxiliary pooled representations. Do not detach the pooled result, because auxiliary score rows must remain trainable. The primary pooled branch is unchanged, and the inherited hidden.detach() score path blocks auxiliary gradients through selectors into keys/targets/actions. All four cells have the same forward function and RNG at matched state; only direct backward paths differ. Supplied standalone variants are both-blocked (candidate), item-blocked, context-blocked and neither-blocked. No future/current labels enter forward.
predictions: Implementation prerequisite for host: at matched seed/state and identical batch, all four cells have identical parameter/state keys, shapes, initial tensors and probabilities within dtype tolerance, in train and evaluation modes. The no-gate cell should reproduce g3-r0002-wide_primary click AUC 0.6583679240765704 and other metrics to host numerical reproducibility tolerance. No-gate mismatch requires an integrity review before interpretation. Verify that context and item/action sources do not alias the same embedding parameter; otherwise the switches identify computation-path ownership only, and the proposed disjoint parameter-group interpretation must be revised before training.

Host backward prerequisite on the same full, mixed, masked and empty-history batches: each single auxiliary BCE has zero/absent gradient to blocked embedding groups and the score trunk, while the corresponding readout row and auxiliary tower retain gradients. In the both-blocked cell all direct auxiliary embedding gradients vanish. A click-only BCE must give matching primary gradients across all four cells at identical state. Non-blocked paths are allowed gradients; nonzero values are not guaranteed on every batch.

If residual embedding interference is consequential, at least one gated cell improves full-population validation click AUC over contemporaneous embedding_joint; 0.0003 absolute AUC is a predeclared practical screening threshold, not a significance threshold. Record smaller positive and negative differences without rounding them to null.

If context and item ownership interact, the difference-in-differences AUC(both)-AUC(context)-AUC(item)+AUC(joint) is nonzero at this seed. Report both simple effects instead of attributing the both-blocked effect to a single group. A positive full-block effect is only controlled local support until repeated.

Report all four tasks AUC/Logloss, click Logloss and auxiliary mean separately; any click gain accompanied by auxiliary loss is a measured tradeoff, not a Pareto improvement or proof of complementary multi-task learning. Compare with aux_detached for descriptive quality/cost context only.

Use the host history bins already defined: empty, 1-16, 17-64, >64 with sample/positive/negative counts and insufficient-slice flags. These effect-by-history checks are exploratory; the bins are fixed but no particular slice gain is predicted. Only use any other slice or paired user-cluster interval if the host exposes authorized train-defined bins or paired predictions/user clusters; do not fabricate them.
falsifiers: Any changed forward information, initial parameters, probability computation, masking behavior, current-action dependence, blocked-path gradient leak or failure to reproduce the no-gate cell invalidates the intended mechanism comparison.

If all gated cells fail to improve click AUC versus embedding_joint, this implementation does not support useful residual embedding ownership under the frozen recipe. Do not conclude that all task-specific embedding mechanisms are refuted.
If only one field gate helps, reject the claim that both groups require click-only ownership. If both improves but the factorial interaction dominates, reject an additive single-group explanation.
If improvements are smaller than 0.0003, unstable under later authorized paired repetitions, or explained by control reproduction variation, retain them as tentative and do not claim robust benefit.

If auxiliary task quality collapses, reject a claim of joint task improvement even if click selection improves. Absent gradient-conflict measurements, do not claim that gains directly establish conflicting gradient directions.
alternative_explanations: One frozen seed and a one-pass recipe establish a local optimization contrast only; seed variation, slower auxiliary convergence and Adagrad accumulator effects remain possible explanations.

Dense gradient clipping is global across tasks and may couple update magnitudes even when direct auxiliary gradients into an embedding group are blocked. No gradient cosine or conflict rate has been measured.

The item gate groups target item fields, history item fields and action values; it cannot attribute an effect to one field or separate target from history. The context group is only the authorized user/context fields, not a new raw user ID.
Item-gated training performs a second pooled matrix multiplication; allocated GPU time and peak memory must be measured. Evaluation without gradients uses one multiplication in all arms.
Auxiliary labels are user/category/brand 24h-window outcomes rather than advertisement-specific conversion attribution; semantic mismatch could matter, but these experiments do not identify it.
Readout/tower optimization, reduced sparse gradient magnitude, implicit regularization or altered finite-pass learning speed can explain any gain without demonstrating semantic preference conflict.

Prior trajectory review: round0 task-feedback retrieval (0.655460783) did not beat initial DIN (0.655544082); item-only task retrieval (0.655881760) did better than the task-feedback arm. In round1, primary selector ownership helped both feedback (+0.002147834) and item-only (+0.001401058) arms versus joint ownership, while auxiliary task outcomes differed. Thus neither feedback inclusion nor routing alone is a universal improvement.

Round2 aux_detached versus aux_live improved click by 0.000635971 and also improved auxiliary AUCs, but aux_detached (0.657420649) did not exceed primary_feedback (0.657608616), aux_frozen (0.657831614), or the near-capacity wide_primary incumbent (0.658367924). Frozen adaptation lost auxiliary quality; width replacement improved click without establishing an auxiliary-adaptation mechanism. Those branches remain negative or tradeoff evidence, not discarded successes.

All supplied prior trials succeeded in execution and have the same frozen single seed; no execution failures or independent repetitions are supplied, and candidate_diagnostics are not_requested. Prior repeated identical joint runs are reproducibility evidence, not independent mechanism or seed evidence. No human-owned/personal knowledge is enabled; no held-out results are available.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Read the original STEM Method and feature-field ablations. Its stop-gradient idea motivates a local ownership test; its benchmark improvements are external and not assumed here.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: One shared table per field, with auxiliary backward ownership switches for context and item/history values. No extra embedding tables or experts.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Field-group backward-only intervention on a target/history selector with fixed forward and capacity; not a reproduction or novelty claim.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: No matched click gain or unacceptable task tradeoff rejects this local adaptation as useful; a static forward or backward mismatch invalidates attribution.

knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Do not credit INFNet for an improvement in these cells; no matched experiment isolates its proxy mechanism.
